correctness.rationale: The scalar Padé quotient at −x is ((x−3)²+3)/((x+3)²+3)>0 and is 1 at x=0, giving positive definiteness, positive diagonal and conservation. The Taylor coefficients satisfy c_j=c_(j−1)/2−c_(j−2)/12 for j≥3: c_1 through c_5 are positive, c_6=0 and c_7=−1/1728. In Q=A−dI, a distance-j geodesic has j! coordinate orders. At distance six the seventh power contributes exactly −7d·6! (one diagonal stay by parity); at distance seven it contributes 7!. This proves the claimed sharp near-zero boundary and coefficients for each fixed d, not a uniform-in-d estimate. At infinity the positive Laplacian eigenvalues give I−12 L†/h+O_d(h⁻²). For an edge, subtract the stationary part of the tensor-product heat kernel and use s=e^(−2t): the Green coefficient is 2^(−d−1) times the integral of [(1−s)(1+s)^(d−1)−1]/s on (0,1). The integral is 1/6 at d=3 and increases strictly thereafter; this controls large-step edges. Independently solving the (d+1)-state distance-shell linear system reproduces exactly the Q_2 and Q_3 formulas, including positive denominators and the two positive nonedge numerators in Q_3. Q_1 follows from the single positive Laplacian eigenvalue; h=0 gives I. Descartes' rule and opposite signs at zero and infinity give exactly one positive zero of the Q_3 edge quartic, approximately 8.583763463733358. value.rationale: The unweighted cube is a natural product graph for diffusion. The result separates loss near zero from loss at large timesteps despite positive eigenvalues and conservation, and gives an exact allowable timestep and sign pattern on the first cube with eventual failure. These are usable matrix-positivity conclusions, not a claim of a new Padé mechanism or a table of isolated tests.
